transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2027-04-05
Time: 15:00 PT (scheduled 45m)
Duration: 42 minutes (recording ended early due to another meeting)
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Alex Gomez (Meridian Head of ML), Priya Kumar (Meridian Platform), Liam O'Neill (Meridian CTO)

Summary: Short walkthrough of Redwood Optimize (batching + KV/prefix cache) with cost model examples. Meridian is evaluating a pilot for payment-approval scoring and customer support summarization. Key asks: latency SLOs < 200ms p95, throughput 500 reqs/s at peak, strict data residency and KMS.

[00:00] Jordan (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Jordan, AE on the account, and with me is Priya our SE. We'll run through Optimize recommendations for batching and the KV/prefix cache cost model. How are you all?
[00:12] Alex (Meridian): Good thanks, Alex here. Short on time so appreciate a focused runthrough. We're mainly trying to understand how caching affects latency and cost for our payment risk scoring and some chat summarization flows.
[00:25] Priya (Redwood SE): Great, we'll do a quick overview then show the numbers 	6 synthetic examples and then what a pilot would look like. Quick question: is your priority cost reduction or hitting p95 latency? or both?
[00:35] Alex: Both but latency is non-negotiable 	6 p95 around 200ms. Cost is a big factor since we expect millions of evals/month.
[00:46] Priya K (Meridian): Also strict data controls: we need KMS integration and audit logs; can you confirm those for the pilot?
[00:54] Jordan: Yes, Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS and audit logs; we'll include the security pack in the docs we send. Liam, anything else on the infra side?
[01:02] Liam: Just that we run in a VPC and might want on-prem options later. For now cloud VPC is fine.

-- Intro to batching and caching --
[01:12] Priya (SE): Alright, quick fundamentals. There are two levers here: batching, which increases GPU throughput by grouping requests 	6 that reduces per-token cost but can add queuing latency; and the prefix/KV cache which avoids recomputation for repeated contexts, often the biggest win for customer support or repeated system messages.
[01:36] Jordan: We split recommendations into config tiers: conservative (low batching, minimal queueing) for strict latency, and aggressive (longer batching windows, larger batch sizes) for max cost savings.
[01:48] Alex: Can you give concrete numbers? like if we have 500 reqs/s what's the tradeoff?
[01:55] Priya (SE): Yes. Example baseline: single-token cost X, baseline latency 120ms p95 for small model on Redwood hosted. If you enable continuous batching at 20ms window and target batch size 32, effective throughput increases and per-token cost drops ~30-35%, p95 goes up to ~160-210ms depending on model and seq length. With prefix/KV cache on typical support flows (70% prefix reuse) we saw token compute drop by ~60-70% 	6 that multiplies cost savings.
[02:26] Alex (interrupt): 70% reuse 	6 that seems high, what's assumed?
[02:29] Priya: Good callout 	6 it's scenario dependent. For templated system prompts and user histories where a lot of the conversation is shared, reuse can be high. We'll baseline from your trace.

-- Cost model walkthrough --
[02:40] Priya (SE): Here's a simple cost model slide 	6 apologies it's rough in the transcript. Scenario A: no cache, conservative batching: cost per 1M tokens = $Y (we'll put real numbers in the doc). Scenario B: conservative batching + prefix cache (50% reuse) = cost ~0.6*Y. Scenario C: aggressive batching + KV cache with hot-keying = cost 0.35*Y. Important: aggressive batching may push p95 past your 200ms SLO for some tails.
[03:10] Jordan: On hardware choices: Dedicated pools with pinned model variants give more predictable latency than shared hosted endpoints. For pilot, many customers start hosted but with dedicated burst or reserved slots for peak windows.
[03:22] Liam: If we go dedicated, does Redwood handle autoscaling?
[03:25] Priya: Yes, dedicated supports autoscaling and burst policies. You can set latency-sensitive nodes and cost-optimized nodes; smart routing sends latency-critical traffic to the latency tier and lower priority to cost tier with fallback.

-- Demo / specific examples --
[03:40] Priya (SE): I'll read out a micro-benchmark we ran against a payment scoring workload: median tokens per request 120, median response tokens 20. Baseline hosted (no cache, batching 0): 140ms median, 180ms p95, cost per 10k requests ~$Z. With prefix cache (prefix reuse 40%), cost lowered by ~38% and p95 improved slightly because cached KV reduces compute. With KV cache and aggressive batching window 30ms, throughput improved 2.6x, cost per 10k requests dropped ~62% but p95 moved to ~260ms.
[04:12] Alex: 260ms p95 is too slow for the scoring path. Could we set a hybrid: hot-path scoring uses no batching or very small batches, while non-critical summarize jobs use aggressive batching?
[04:24] Priya: Exactly 	6 routing policies can split by route or header. You can mark scoring endpoints as latency-critical and attach a strict batching policy (e.g., max wait 5ms, small batch size). Summarization endpoints can use larger windows.
[04:36] Jordan: And the KV cache can be shared across both tiers where appropriate; the hot-path can use KV lookup only (very low latency) if the prefix exists, otherwise fallback to live model.

-- Data residency / security discussion --
[04:50] Liam: For SOC2 and KMS, we need to verify auditability and that keys never leave our account. Do you have a SOC2 plus an option for customer-managed KMS?
[04:58] Jordan: Redwood is SOC2 Type II. For Private deployments or VPCs we support customer-managed KMS and HSM integrations; keys can be in your cloud account and we can provide logs. We'll attach security docs.
[05:10] Priya K: Also need encryption in transit and at rest 	6 includes KV cache encryption?
[05:14] Priya (SE): Yes 	6 KV cache is encrypted at rest; for Private it uses your KMS. For hosted we use our encryption with options for BYOK in the Private plan.

-- Micro-benchmark and pilot design --
[05:25] Priya (SE): For the pilot we'd propose: 1) ingest anonymized trace to profile token distribution 2) run a 1-week KV cache micro-benchmark with sample traffic 3) provision a small dedicated lane for latency-critical scoring and a cost lane for batch workloads 4) measure cost/latency and tune batch windows and cache TTLs.
[05:45] Alex: Timeboxed 	6 how much effort on our side?
[05:48] Priya (SE): For step 1, just an export of request timestamps and token counts 	6 we can supply the script. Step 2 requires a proxy or route to send replay traffic 	6 we can run in a non-prod environment. We estimate engineering effort 1-2 days to set up replay.
[06:02] Jordan: We'll share the micro-benchmark template and a sample output (Priya will share).

-- Q&A and misc clarifications --
[06:10] Alex: A few quick technicals 	6 what's the KV cache eviction strategy and consistency model?
[06:15] Priya (SE): By default LRU with configurable TTLs; strong read-after-write is not required for these caches 	6 it's eventual but very fast. For strict consistency you can configure synchronous writes but that's a performance cost.
[06:28] Priya K: Any per-route RBAC for who can flush caches?
[06:32] Jordan: Console has per-route roles and you can expose cache controls to admins only. Audit logs will show flush/evictions.
[06:40] Alex: How does prefix cache differ from KV cache?
[06:44] Priya (SE): Prefix cache stores the model's KV states for common prefixes so you avoid recomputing the prefix. KV cache here we mean the same concept (we sometimes call it prefix/KV). There's also a higher-level application cache that stores full responses. We recommend using prefix/KV for internal repeated contexts and response cache for idempotent outputs.
[06:58] Alex: Ok. Any gotchas with multi-tenant models? we will multi-tenant some services initially.
[07:04] Priya (SE): For multi-tenant, we namespace KV by tenant; memory requirements grow with number of hot keys, but hit rates often justify cost. Also, cache warming strategies help on deployment rollouts.

-- Pricing and unit economics example --
[07:18] Jordan: Quick numbers (example, not a quote): Baseline per-1M tokens hosted $120, with conservative batching $85, with 50% prefix reuse $45, with aggressive batching+KV $28. These are illustrative; we'll produce a spreadsheet tied to your token mix and peak throughput.
[07:36] Alex: Those are helpful. Please include a breakdown by CPU/GPU hours, storage for KV, and networking.
[07:41] Priya: Will do. The KV storage is small compared to compute for large seq loads, but for huge numbers of unique prefixes storage matters 	6 we'll model both.

-- Transcript imperfections / misc notes --
[07:55] (background noise / someone dropping off briefly)
[08:00] Priya (SE): I'll also call out that quantization can reduce compute cost too 	6 if you have floating point sensitive tasks, we'll recommend model variants that trade off a tiny quality delta for large perf gains.
[08:13] Liam: We need a quality gate 	6 any regression detection you provide?
[08:16] Jordan: Redwood Optimize includes quality monitoring tied to eval prompt sets; we can set up regression alerts on key prompts and integrate into your CI.

-- Final recap and next steps --
[08:26] Jordan: To recap: 1) We'll send pilot proposal + pricing; 2) Priya will share micro-benchmark template and sample results; 3) Meridian to export sample traces; 4) schedule pilot kickoff tentatively 2027-04-12.
[08:40] Alex: Sounds good. One ask: can you include a short table that maps batching window + batch size -> expected p95 impact so we can pick safe defaults?
[08:49] Priya: Yes 	6 we'll include that matrix. Also we'll highlight routing policy examples for hybrid lanes.
[08:55] Jordan: Great. We'll follow up with security docs and a short implementation checklist for the pilot.
[09:02] (meeting ends, recording stopped)

Notes: Transcript is roughly accurate but contains some auto-transcription errors (K-V cash, pre-fix). Attendees asked for concrete micro-benchmark data and a pilot plan. Redwood to provide pricing spreadsheet and bench template.
